chapter: Chapter II: Coherent Sheaves and Analytic Spaces

examples.title: Presheaves and Sheaves
examples.content: A presheaf assigns to each open set U a group F(U) of sections, with restriction maps. A sheaf additionally satisfies local-to-global compatibility axioms.

examples.title: Sheaf Axioms
examples.content: For any open cover {Uᵢ} of U: (1) If s|ᵤᵢ = t|ᵤᵢ for all i, then s = t. (2) Given compatible local sections sᵢ, there exists a global section s with s|ᵤᵢ = sᵢ.

simulator.title: Locally Trivial Sheaf
simulator.description: A sheaf can be visualized as sections over a base space. The torus represents a space over which we study sheaves.

applications.title: Algebraic Geometry
applications.description: Sheaves of regular functions and coherent sheaves are fundamental in scheme theory.

applications.title: Topology
applications.description: Sheaf cohomology provides powerful invariants for topological spaces.

concepts.name: Presheaf
concepts.definition: A contravariant functor from open sets of X to a category (e.g., abelian groups).

concepts.name: Stalk
concepts.definition: The direct limit Fₓ = lim F(U) over all open neighborhoods U of x.

exercises.question: Show that the constant presheaf ℤ (assigning ℤ to every open set) is not a sheaf on disconnected spaces.
exercises.hint: Consider a space with two connected components.

exercises.question: Prove that the sheafification of a presheaf is unique up to isomorphism.
exercises.hint: Use the universal property of sheafification.

diagrams.title: Sections Over Open Sets
diagrams.description: Visualize how local sections patch together to form global sections.
diagrams.instructions: Each region represents an open set with its local section.
